SELECTED_INDEX: 4
CONFIDENCE: 0.55
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows only aliphatic C–H stretches at 2887, 2946 and 2964 cm⁻¹ with no aromatic C–H region, so the molecule is aliphatic.  Key fingerprint bands match typical sulfonyl / sulfamate vibrations: 
• νas(SO₂) 1323–1357 cm⁻¹ (peaks 1323, 1357)  
• νs(SO₂) ~1130 cm⁻¹ (peak 1134)  
• N–S / N–O stretch near 915 cm⁻¹ (peak 919)  
• C–S stretch 690–730 cm⁻¹ (peak 691)  
• Additional SO₂ / C–S deformation near 770–830 cm⁻¹ (peaks 771, 801, 826)  
These features are characteristic of a sulfonamide/sulfamate such as CC(C)COS(=O)(=O)NO (candidate 4).  Peaks at 1453 cm⁻¹ (CH₃/CH₂ bending) and the strong aliphatic C–H stretches fit its isopropyl/ethyl chain.  No carbonyl (∼1700 cm⁻¹) or strong NH/OH stretches (>3100 cm⁻¹) are required, consistent with candidate 4 (only an N-O bond, no free OH).  Other candidates either contain aromatic rings (would give 1600 cm⁻¹ bands) or carbonyl groups that are absent here.
